html:
The Ineseño are the Chumash people of the Santa Ynez valley, inland from Santa Barbara in California. Their name comes from Mission Santa Inés, and they call themselves Samala. Their language, Ineseño or Samala, is one of the Chumashan languages.

Before the Spanish came they lived in villages along the Santa Ynez River, gathered acorns, hunted and traded with coastal Chumash, who fished from plank canoes.

The Spanish founded Mission Santa Inés in 1804, and many Ineseño were brought to live and work there. In 1824 the Chumash revolt against the missions began at Santa Inés and spread to La Purísima and Santa Barbara. The Santa Ynez Band of Chumash Indians now has a small reservation in the valley. Their neighbours to the north were the Salinan, and to the east the Tongva.
